To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acousto-optical diffraction efficiency of the crystal is proportional to the square of the acoustic wave amplitude, the acoustic wave frequency, the optical wave wavelength, the square of the refractive index of the crystal and inversely proportional to the square root of the crystal mass density.

(i) a single acousto-optical interaction can be described as an optical diffraction of the light beam by an acoustic beam and (ii) a double interaction can be described either as an acousto-opto-acoustic interaction (in the case of an acousto-electric interaction) or as a double optical diffraction (in the case other types of interactions).

1) acousto-optical effects are of a general nature and are present in all materials, 2) the acousto-optically induced refractive index changes are the most efficient, 3) the acoustical wave velocity is the highest and, therefore, the highest diffraction efficiency is achieved, and 4) the highest efficiency is obtained when the acoustic and optical beams are parallel.
